title: Qin's First Emperor Orders the Books Burned
dek: In 213 BC the chancellor Li Si persuades the First Emperor to burn private copies of the Odes, the Documents and rival states' histories. Historians still argue over how much burned.
body: Han tradition says the scholar Fu Sheng hid the Book of Documents in a wall. When he dug it out after Qin fell, 29 chapters survived.

panels.label: Chunyu Yue Said
panels.text: Chunyu Yue said no state had lasted long without taking antiquity as its teacher, and urged the emperor to give fiefs to his sons and brothers.

panels.label: Li Si Said
panels.text: Li Si said times had changed, that scholars studied the past to criticize the present and confuse the people, and that their books should burn.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: Each man said he was guarding the dynasty; at stake was who could judge the emperor’s rule, scholars reading old books or officials teaching the new law.
